presentation.label: Temp Save
presentation.summary: FUNC + YES keeps a temporary copy of the active pattern and its Part; FUNC + NO puts both back, as Temp Save and Reload do on the Digitakt and Digitone.
presentation.overview: Got a groove you like? Press FUNC + YES to keep a temporary copy of the pattern and its whole Part, scenes included, from the pattern screen or from almost any page or menu. Experiment freely, then press FUNC + NO to bring both back at once, even while the sequencer plays. The copy is separate from the saved Part and the copy/paste clipboard, so RELOAD PART and pattern paste work as before.
highlights: One gesture keeps the pattern (trigs, locks, length, scale) and the whole active Part: machines, every page, both effects and the scenes.
FUNC + NO restores both at once, also while playing; the crossfader, the selected scenes and the mutes stay where your hands left them.
Separate from the saved Part and the clipboard: RELOAD PART still goes back to your last Part save, and copied patterns or tracks stay on the clipboard.
On another pattern, bank or project FUNC + NO shows NO TEMP SAVE and changes nothing.
Works from the pattern screen and from page and menu windows; sample lists keep their FUNC + YES preview, and dialogs and editors are left alone.
usage: On the pattern screen, or in a SETUP page, MIXER or another menu, press FUNC + YES: TEMP SAVED.
Change the pattern and the Part as you like: trigs, knobs, scenes, machines.
Press FUNC + NO: RELOADED. The pattern and its Part are back as they were at FUNC + YES.

limitations: OS 1.40C. Tested by hand on one MKII over USB; the MKI and the card build were not run on a unit.
One temporary copy, of one pattern and its Part, kept in the module's memory: gone after a power-off and never written to the card. Save the Part and the project to keep your work.

FUNC + YES and FUNC + NO no longer repeat ARM ALL and DISARM ALL on the pattern screen and in page and menu windows; YES and NO alone still do. In sample lists (FUNC + YES still previews), an audio track's SRC SETUP, AED, dialogs, RENAME, TEMPO and CHOOSE PROJECT both gestures stay stock.
The reload replaces the pattern and the Part as a whole, including edits made since FUNC + YES on any track; the Part then counts as edited, as after a paste.
Another project, or this one saved under another name, makes the copy unusable (NO TEMP SAVE).
Uses 892 bytes of code and a 42,892-byte buffer; over USB from the module pool all modules share.

storage.label: Storage
storage.display: 892 B of code plus a 42,892 B copy buffer; no DSP code, no saved data
storage.conditions: The published USB package: 892 bytes of code and data (6 relocations), 42,892 bytes of bss. On the card build the unit sits in the platform's DRAM reserve.

processing.label: CPU / DSP load
processing.display: None while idle; ~16k instructions a save, ~640k a reload (emulator)
processing.conditions: ot_emu, executed instructions from the hook's entry, interrupts included: a save to its toast 16,287 (up to 39,151 under a MIDI flood), a reload to the end of its screen refresh 637,251 stopped and 640,923 playing; no DSP work. Under a MIDI flood the longest frame interrupt rose 0.3 us and idle fell 0.2 points against stock. Time on the unit not measured.

impact.conditions: One reload while the sequencer plays; nothing runs between presses.

cpu.rationale: No idle cost. A save copies about 43 KB (16,287 executed instructions under ot_emu); a reload runs stock's pattern writer, Part Reload and screen refresh (about 640,000 instructions, most of them stock's). Time on the unit is not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code. The restored Part reaches the DSP through stock's own Part apply, as RELOAD PART does.

memory.rationale: A 42,892-byte buffer for one pattern and one Part, plus 892 bytes of code: on USB about a sixth of the 256 KB module pool all modules share; no saved data.

tests.summary: On one MKII over USB (28 Oct 2026), by hand on the flashed base: save and reload on the pattern screen and in eleven page and menu windows, stock FUNC + YES/NO kept in SRC SETUP, both sample lists, AED, a yes/no dialog and RENAME; earlier sources also covered machine and Part changes, quick double presses, menus, YES/NO alone and FUNC + CUE. Under ot_emu (verify.py, 54 checks MKII, 45 MKI): the pattern and Part restored byte for byte in RAM and their battery copies, every page and menu window, each stock-only case, Part switch, bank without saved Parts, MIDI mode, power cycle; beside Apply Scene, Preview Vol and Direct Jump.

license.declaration: Original authored source by Nathaniel Pavel (@npp1993). Stock code is referenced by address, length and SHA-256 only. No firmware, extracted stock routine or table, image, card or memory dump is included.

access.location: The pattern screen and every page or menu window (SETUP pages, MIXER, PART, PROJECT, ARRANGER and more); not sample lists, an audio track's SRC SETUP, AED, dialogs or editors.
steps: Hold FUNC and press YES: TEMP SAVED keeps a copy of the active pattern and its Part.
Edit the pattern and the Part as you like.
Hold FUNC and press NO: RELOADED puts the copy back. On another pattern FUNC + NO shows NO TEMP SAVE.
Save the Part and the project to keep the result.
